evals.name: preflight-reports-before-spending
evals.expected_output: Prints the preflight report with cli_version read from claude --version, floor_met, platform, sandbox_backend, target_type: plugin, suite_tools, estimate_usd, and ceiling, then stops. No claude plugin eval invocation happens during a preflight.
expectations: Every preflight field is printed, including sandbox_backend and estimate_usd
cli_version comes from reading claude --version rather than being asserted
target_type is reported as plugin for a directory holding a plugin manifest and an eval dir
No eval run is launched and no cost is incurred by the preflight action

evals.name: windows-refuses-bash-granting-case
evals.prompt: /evals:plugin-eval run ./my-plugin. One of the cases has allowed_tools: [Bash, Read] and I'm on native Windows.
evals.expected_output: Refuses before invoking the CLI: reports sandbox_backend: absent for native Windows, explains that each Bash-granting run would be refused rather than run unconfined so the case reports a run error and scores nothing, and names the route (WSL2, a Linux host with bubblewrap and socat, macOS, or a Claude cloud session).
expectations: Refuses before any claude plugin eval invocation, so no money is spent
Names the missing sandbox backend as the reason rather than a generic failure
Names at least one working route: WSL2, Linux with bubblewrap and socat, macOS, or a cloud session
Does not suggest running the suite unconfined or stripping the sandbox

evals.name: rules-target-refused-with-pointer
evals.prompt: /evals:plugin-eval run .claude/rules. I want to measure whether our rules actually change the model's behavior.
evals.expected_output: Reports target_type: rules and refuses: every run starts from a throwaway home with CLAUDE.md, rules, settings, memory, and other plugins absent, so a shim that re-injects the rule would measure the shim. Routes to /claude-config:unhobble when the claude-config plugin is installed, and otherwise describes the bare-baseline experiment in a sentence.
expectations: Refuses the rules target rather than scaffolding an append_system_prompt workaround
States that the harness strips rules from every run as the reason
Routes to claude-config:unhobble behind an installed-ness gate with a stated fallback

evals.name: unlimited-prints-estimate-and-proceeds
evals.prompt: /evals:plugin-eval run plugins/evals. I have set the unlimited cost option, so don't stop to ask me anything.
evals.expected_output: Prints the cost estimate anyway (cases x runs x arms plus three judge calls per paid grader per run, carried as roughly), drops --max-cost-usd from the invocation, and starts the run with no confirmation prompt.
expectations: The estimate is printed even though the ceiling is unlimited
No confirmation prompt is raised before the run starts
The invocation omits --max-cost-usd rather than passing a large number

evals.name: validator-runs-before-the-command
evals.expected_output: Runs the static case validator first (validate-cases.py under the plugin root, resolving to plugins/evals/skills/validate/scripts/validate-cases.py in this repository), treats exit 1 as a stop with a route to /evals:validate, and only invokes claude plugin eval with the target ahead of --json, --tag, and --allow-tools once validation passes.
expectations: The validator is run before any paid invocation
A validator FAIL stops the run instead of spending on broken cases
The CLI invocation puts the target before the list-taking flags

evals.name: partial-result-not-read-as-a-score
evals.prompt: /evals:plugin-eval read results.json. The suite exited 2 and the JSON has partial: true with partialReason: cost_ceiling.
evals.expected_output: Reads partial first, reports that the suite did not finish and its scores belong in no trend, and does not report a delta or a suite score as if the run were complete.
expectations: partial is checked before any score is reported
Names cost_ceiling as the reason the run is incomplete
Does not present a suite score or delta as a result of the run

evals.name: skipped-graders-and-omitted-delta
evals.prompt: /evals:plugin-eval read results.json. Partial is false and it exited 0, but one case has no delta field and one without-run has skippedPaidGraders: true.
evals.expected_output: Explains that the ceiling skipped judge calls rather than runs, so a pass can end partial: false with exit 0 and one case still incomparable; reports that case as not comparable rather than reading the omitted delta as zero, and reports the other cases normally.
expectations: The omitted delta is never reported or computed as zero
The skippedPaidGraders run is named as the reason the arms are not comparable
Explains that the ceiling skips judge calls, not runs

evals.name: both-arms-perfect-is-a-null-result
evals.prompt: /evals:plugin-eval read results.json. Every case scored 1.00 with the plugin and 1.00 without it. Great result, right?
evals.expected_output: States that a case at 1.00 in both arms proves the plugin contributed nothing to that case: it is a passing case and a null measurement at once. Routes to grading terms the plugin's own surfaces supply, and to pairing a result grader with a process grader, rather than celebrating the score.
expectations: Does not present a zero delta as evidence the plugin works
Explains that equal arms mean the plugin contributed nothing to those cases
Suggests a concrete authoring fix rather than only naming the problem

evals.name: skill-creator-format-routed-elsewhere
evals.prompt: /evals:plugin-eval validate my skill's evals/evals.json before I run it.
evals.expected_output: Names the format boundary: evals/evals.json is the skill-creator format and is not interchangeable with the plugin eval case layout, so it routes to /skill-quality:check validate-evals when the skill-quality plugin is installed and states the fallback when it is not; it does not run the plugin eval case validator against it.
expectations: Distinguishes the skill-creator evals.json format from the case format this skill runs
Routes to skill-quality:check validate-evals behind an installed-ness gate
Does not claim to validate or run the evals.json file itself

evals.name: natural-language-trigger
evals.prompt: I rewrote the description on one of our skills and I want to know whether the model actually picks it up now, and whether that change made anything worse. We have a plugin with some eval cases already.
evals.expected_output: Triggers from natural language with no slash command: routes to preflight and the run flow, explains that the with-versus-without delta is the number that answers the question, and names the canonical first finding (a delta near zero with the tool_used: Skill grader failing means the description, not the case, is the fix).
expectations: Triggers without the user typing /evals:plugin-eval
Starts from preflight and the cost estimate rather than invoking the CLI immediately
Frames the answer as the ablation delta rather than an absolute score
